entrypoints.summary: The lab directs modification of the request's product category filter parameter.
The affected request parameter is named category.

negative_controls: No actual negative-control response or test-run result is included in the bundle.
observability.positive_marker: One or more unreleased products are displayed.

preconditions: The documented lab contains a SQL injection vulnerability in its product category filter.
The attacker can modify the HTTP request that sets the category filter.

trigger_steps.summary: Intercept and modify the category-filter request, then submit a category value that injects a true OR expression and comments out trailing SQL.

mitigations.concept: fixed SQL predicate structure for category filtering

relation_candidates.rationale: The documented category payload contains SQL OR and comment syntax that is processed in the query context.
The documented true OR expression and comment marker change the intended category-and-released predicate.
The lab defines success as displaying one or more unreleased products.

relation_candidates.dst: fixed SQL predicate structure for category filtering
relation_candidates.rationale: Keeping category data from altering SQL syntax preserves the released-only predicate described by the lab.

impact.affected_asset: Unreleased product data in the products table.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause the category-filter query to return products outside the intended released-only result set.
impact.security_effect: Unauthorized disclosure of hidden, unreleased product records in the application response.

causal_trace.summary: A remote user controls the category value used by the product category filter.
The supplied category text is interpreted as SQL syntax: the documented value '+OR+1=1-- adds a true disjunct and comments out the remainder of the WHERE predicate.
The application executes a products SELECT whose intended predicate is category = 'Gifts' AND released = 1; injected SQL changes the predicate evaluated by the database.
The modified query can cause the response to display one or more unreleased products.

failure.operation: Database evaluation of the category-filter SELECT WHERE predicate after attacker-controlled SQL syntax is incorporated.

primary_invariant.statement: A category-filter request must preserve the products-query restriction that only rows with released = 1 are returned.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Attacker-controlled category content is accepted as part of the SQL expression, so an OR 1=1 expression and SQL comment marker can neutralize the released restriction.

quality.review_notes: This is a deliberately vulnerable PortSwigger training lab, not a versioned production advisory or a code/patch review. The page supplies a request modification and an oracle contract but no captured execution result. No remediation implementation or patch is present; the remediation statement is limited to the predicate-integrity invariant implied by the documented mechanism.

remediation.invariant_restored: The category value can select a category but cannot add predicates or comment out the released = 1 restriction.
mitigation_classes: Preserve fixed SQL predicate structure by preventing category input from being interpreted as SQL syntax

affected_versions_or_commits.value: Observed 2026-07-16; official lab page has no explicit content version

target.component: product category filter and products query
target.project_or_package: PortSwigger Web Security Academy SQL injection lab

oracle.expected_negative: A non-injecting category-filter request should retain the documented released = 1 condition; the bundle provides no observed negative-control response.
oracle.expected_positive: After submitting a request with category value '+OR+1=1--, the lab's documented success condition is that the response contains one or more unreleased products.
